actors: The licensed firm filing the assessed STR: a licensed corporation, SFC-licensed virtual asset service provider or associated entity within the circular's collective definition.
The JFIU, which receives the STR through STREAMS 2.
Hongkong Post, identified as the provider of the required e-Cert for XML and prescribed PDF submissions.
objects: STREAMS 2 as the reporting channel, distinct from the submission format.
An XML representation of the STR.
A completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format.
The web-based STR form within STREAMS 2.
A Hongkong Post e-Cert associated with the assessed XML or PDF submission.
The separately provided JFIU XML schema and the technical test arrangements.
relationships: The licensed firm submits the STR to the JFIU through a channel using a particular submission method.
XML and prescribed PDF are alternative submission methods within STREAMS 2; neither is itself an alternative reporting channel.
The footnote 3 marker attaches the e-Cert requirement separately to the XML and PDF alternatives.
The web-based alternative has no footnote 3 marker in the retained source.
The XML schema and technical test arrangements are additional XML-related requirements, distinct from selecting XML as the submission format.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One submission event by one classified licensed firm for one STR, assessed only against the selected channel, submission-method and footnote 3 certificate requirements.
proposals.temporal_basis: The ordinary submission rule is assessed from the stated launch at 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The blackout begins at 12:00am on 28 January 2026 and ends at that launch. A submission before 9:00am on 2 February is not brought into the ordinary rule merely because its calendar date is 2 February. The source does not expressly identify the timezone.
classification_assumptions: The filing entity is classified separately under the circular's definition of licensed firms; no classification is inferred from its use of STREAMS 2.
The specific 9:00am launch and resumption provision determines the post-launch boundary for this model when read with the general effective-date provision.
Each assessed event has an identifiable submission method; a later resubmission is a separate event.
Footnote 3 applies to the XML and PDF alternatives carrying its marker. No e-Cert requirement for the web-based alternative is inferred from this footnote.
Certificate satisfaction means that a Hongkong Post e-Cert is supplied or used for this particular submission in the required manner; mere firm-level possession does not establish that fact.

The result covers only the selected channel, method and certificate requirements. It does not decide the STR's substantive adequacy, filing timeliness, XML schema conformity, technical testing or overall legal compliance.

reading.subject: Post-launch channel, submission method and method-specific e-Cert requirements
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] For an in-scope post-launch submission by a classified licensed firm, true means that the STR was submitted to the JFIU through STREAMS 2 using XML with the required Hongkong Post e-Cert, a completed prescribed PDF form with that e-Cert, or the completed STREAMS 2 web-based STR form. False means that at least one of these selected requirements was not met. An unknown input remains unknown, and an out-of-scope event receives no compliance verdict. This answers only whether the assessed submission meets the selected channel, method and footnote 3 requirements; it confers no legal approval.
reading.distinction: A single fact such as electronic_submission would conceal the distinction between channel and format, while firm_has_ecert would conceal the submission-specific certificate requirement. XML and PDF require both the STREAMS 2 channel and the footnote 3 certificate condition. The retained text does not attach that certificate condition to the web-based alternative. The blackout is excluded from this ordinary post-launch rule.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2. Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2

licensed firms that intend to submit STRs via the XML format are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU and liaise with it as soon as possible to arrange a technical test to ensure a smooth transition.

assumptions: The filing entity is classified separately under the circular's definition of licensed firms; no classification is inferred from its use of STREAMS 2.
The specific 9:00am launch and resumption provision determines the post-launch boundary for this model when read with the general effective-date provision.
Each assessed event has an identifiable submission method; a later resubmission is a separate event.
Footnote 3 applies to the XML and PDF alternatives carrying its marker. No e-Cert requirement for the web-based alternative is inferred from this footnote.
Certificate satisfaction means that a Hongkong Post e-Cert is supplied or used for this particular submission in the required manner; mere firm-level possession does not establish that fact.

The result covers only the selected channel, method and certificate requirements. It does not decide the STR's substantive adequacy, filing timeliness, XML schema conformity, technical testing or overall legal compliance.

reading.subject: Resubmission trigger distinguished from blackout contact and subsequent discharge
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] True means that the assessed licensed firm's STR has at least one submission to the JFIU through a channel other than STREAMS 2 following implementation, so the stated requirement to resubmit that STR through STREAMS 2 is triggered. False means that no such qualifying submission exists in the established event history. Unknown or incomplete event history must not be treated as false. This answers whether the resubmission trigger occurred, not whether the firm has complied with or discharged the obligation. Separately, an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout calls for direct JFIU contact by email, phone or fax; that instruction is not evaluated by this trigger. These proposed meanings confer no legal approval.
reading.distinction: Reviewing the submission-event model exposes a missing relation between multiple events concerning the same STR. A single off_platform Boolean would conflate urgent blackout contact, a post-launch alternative-channel submission and an automatically migrated old record. Only the second supplies the stated footnote 2 trigger. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission cannot make the original event comply with the exclusive-channel requirement, and the fact that a trigger occurred does not establish an outstanding or overdue obligation.

For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2. The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.

facts.meaning: The entity responsible for the assessed STR is a licensed corporation, SFC-licensed virtual asset service provider or associated entity within the circular's collective definition.
facts.unit: Boolean classification of the responsible entity

facts.name: report_has_postlaunch_other_channel_submission
facts.meaning: There exists at least one actual submission of this same STR to the JFIU through a channel other than STREAMS 2 at or after 9:00am on 2 February 2026 in the governing timezone. Direct contact alone and automatic migration do not count as submissions. True requires evidence of a qualifying event; false requires an established history sufficient to rule out such an event. This externally supplied factual aggregate expresses the event quantifier absent from the formula language.
facts.unit: Boolean existence predicate over one STR's submission history

unresolved: No prior proposals were supplied. The consequential challenge to the first proposal is the second proposal's report-level event history, which adds event identity, an existential quantifier and timing rather than manufacturing a conflicting interpretation.

The blackout urgent-contact instruction is preserved explicitly, but these two bounded results do not separately evaluate its satisfaction. A further predicate would need the STR's urgent-submission classification during the blackout and evidence of direct JFIU contact by at least one listed method.

The retained text does not specify the operational use of an e-Cert. The certificate fact must remain unknown until that requirement and the submission evidence establish it; possession alone cannot be substituted.

The formal language lacks timestamps and event quantifiers. The proposals therefore declare explicit temporal and event-history facts whose underlying evidence must be assessed externally; no date-only comparison or invented fact value substitutes for that evidence.
A determination that a resubmission obligation is outstanding, overdue or discharged needs additional facts and any applicable JFIU guidance. The trigger model does not answer those questions.
The four listed missing dependencies have no supplied contents. Their implications, the separately provided XML schema, technical test details and subsequent resubmission guidance remain unexamined.
